expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: no. The test you added would have passed every one of those three weeks."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "COALESCE(amount, 0) converts 'this row failed to join' into 'this row earned $0'. The pipeline cannot distinguish a missing value from a legitimate zero"

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation: daily SUM(revenue) vs. the billing system / ledger, within tolerance."

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "build to staging → test staging → promote on pass" and "A test that runs after publication and emails someone is the same three weeks with a nicer log."

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Data contract on the upstream table: pin the columns you depend on; CI on their repo fails on rename, or your ingest fails loudly on schema mismatch."

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Join-integrity assertion: COUNT(*) WHERE joined_key IS NULL ≤ a small threshold" and "Volume floor against same-weekday history"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: "Why 'not empty' can't catch it" section frames detection gap; "Class sweep (do this before closing)" treats as systematic issue

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Shows that shape-based tests can't catch logic errors and that silent wrongness produces "plausible but low" results, but does not explicitly explain why this is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
